time_reference.reason: Existing fixed Calendar timestamp reference and compatible framework ^3.8.4 dependency; actual installed source used, not an assumed latest version.
time_reference.locale: Reference default en, not a claim that the complete Carbon locale/cascade SDK exists.

invariants: Only integer 2 means FAIL and integer 3 means SKIPPED; float/string 2 and false mean DONE.
No callback means no duration formatting. Callback executes once even when verbosity suppresses output.
Callback Result error writes FAIL before propagating; formatting failure during finally supersedes callback failure. Native panic is rendered and resumed.
Selected output identity, formatter, physical stderr/stdout and nested newline counts preserved; callback receives safe reborrow of same selected output.

Description strips one final punctuation and paths through existing mutators. Width counts Unicode scalar values before formatting, not terminal column width; regex intentionally excludes hyphens like fixed source.
Dots are individually styled, layout cap150 does not truncate content, COLUMNS0/8/40/80/200 run in separate real processes.

Default duration <=1000ms uses existing PHP half-up code extended to precision2, sign/zero and grouping preserved. Longer output uses fixed default cascades and whole seconds; nan/positive_inf/negative_inf use actual source strings.
adaptations: Native method split expresses optional callback/verbosity without overloading. Return T uses explicit Into<Value>, not arbitrary implicit object serialization. Native TaskResult converts to its integer backing (source ->value); source enum object identity is not represented by this conversion.
Callback receives mutable OutputReference instead of implicit PHP $this alias. FnOnce prevents repeated execution and Rust borrow checking prevents stream aliasing.
Duration override uses per-component Send callback composition; default wording follows source default en, custom wording supplied explicitly. Full date/locale/cascade SDK is not delivered here.

SystemTime supplies wall epoch seconds and supports times on either side of epoch. Native OS resolution may exceed PHP microseconds; actual elapsed output is checked by units, deterministic explicit start/end by exact source bytes.

Unrepresentable explicit duration magnitudes return ConsoleError rather than unchecked integer conversion; ordinary system-time task ranges and measured fixed vectors verified. PHP engine diagnostics are not replayed.
